headline: Big 5 Construct Saudi Opens Today: The Agenda for Four Days in Riyadh
deck: Five overlapping shows, a nine-stream conference programme and a curated sustainability trail give the Riyadh Front week its structure.
excerpt: Big 5 Construct Saudi opened at Riyadh Front for a four-day run to 2 September, with more than 1,000 exhibitors from over 50 countries and four co-located shows covering heavy equipment, concrete, HVACR and facilities management. A nine-stream conference programme and the Big 5 Impact Trail run alongside the exhibition halls.
content:
Big 5 Construct Saudi opened this morning at the Riyadh Front Exhibition and Conference Center for a four-day run to 2 September, bringing more than 1,000 exhibitors from over 50 countries under the patronage of the Ministry of Industry and Mineral Resources. The organiser's stated expectation is upwards of 35,000 trade visitors across the four days.

The show is not a single exhibition but five overlapping ones. Heavy Saudi Arabia, Totally Concrete Saudi Arabia, HVACR Saudi Arabia and Saudi FM & Clean all run co-located with the main event, which gives the week its structure: earthworks and machinery, materials and mix production, building systems and cooling, and then the operation and cleaning of the finished asset. The organiser's framing for the edition is "From foundation to future, built for every scale", and the sector spread reflects it, running from general construction and concrete through heavy equipment, HVACR and facilities management.

That structure matters more than it sounds. Saudi Arabia's construction market is large enough that its segments have started to move at different speeds, and a visitor's four days are best spent according to where their exposure sits. Contractors chasing earthmoving capacity and lifting have a different show to a developer trying to work out how a completed district gets maintained for the next thirty years.

Running through the halls is a conference programme built around nine topic areas: codes, standards and regulations; health and safety; sustainability; artificial intelligence; technology; project management; concrete; modular construction; and HVACR. The sessions are framed around problems rather than products, including navigating the Saudi Building Code, improving concrete quality, strengthening project governance, applying artificial intelligence in project delivery, and improving coordination between HVACR design, installation and facilities management teams.

The organisations on the speaking list are a reasonable proxy for who the show is aimed at. They include the Saudi Building Code Center, ROSHN Group, SEVEN, Misk City, Saudi Binladin Group, Al Kholi Group, Modern Building Leaders, Kabbani Construction Group and Dussman Ajlan & Bros, a mix of regulator, giga-project developer, contractor and facilities operator. Two named speakers are confirmed in the programme: Christopher Seymour, managing director for the Middle East and Africa at Mace Consult, and Shonagh Kinnaird MCIOB, project director at Misk City. Their sessions examine collaboration between stakeholders, digital transparency, procurement challenges, and the lessons carried out of Saudi Arabia's major developments.

Alongside the conference, the Big 5 Impact Trail runs as a curated route through the halls, spotlighting products and systems selected for low-impact technology, circular-economy principles and operational sustainability. Solutions on the trail this year include Masdar's Kronospan carbon-negative wood-based panels and engineered boards, Galaxy Technology's Albion Valves range with carbon transparency across its cast-iron products, Star Factory's spray polyurethane foam roofing and waterproofing system, ground improvement and foundation work from Keller, and integrated facilities and energy management from Al-Futtaim Engineering.

For buyers, the practical value of the week is comparison. A large share of what is on the floor is a physical product with a specification sheet, and the halls allow a procurement team to put two competing systems side by side, inspect build quality, question a technical specialist and check certification in an afternoon. That is a hard exercise to replicate through a supplier portal.

The market context is supportive without being uncomplicated. Saudi construction output is forecast to grow 6.2 per cent this year to around SAR 232.14 billion, and the Saudi Contractors Authority logged 18 awards worth more than SR 30.03 billion in May, the highest monthly value of 2026, and 25 awards worth over SR 29.5 billion in June. Rising costs and re-phasing across parts of the giga-project programme are the counterweight, and they are likely to shape a good deal of the conversation in the aisles.

The exhibition runs daily until 2 September at Riyadh Front, with the full exhibitor list and session timings published by the organiser.
